text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.

- State oil company INA faces losing a $60 million export deal with Bosnian Federation, following an ultimatum by its Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic who made oil deliveries conditional upon Croatia' purchase of electricity and coal from the Federation.
- President Tudjman calls on all the citizens living in Eastern Slavonia region to go to the polls on Sunday, April 13.
- The military has met all the conditions for Croatia to join NATO, says Defence Minister Gojko Susak in an interview.
- American oil company Texaco starts negotiations with local partners on the joint opening of 50-70 petrol stations across Croatia in the next five years.
- Some 456 motorists may have to go back to driving school due to traffic offences.
- A third of the citizens of Zagreb are still undecided about who to vote for in the upcoming local elections.
- We have not made a single wrong move, says head of the government's transitional office in Osijek, Ivica Vrkic.
- Italy will pay eight cents per square meter of natural gas, or four cents less than the price on the international market, under an agreement between INA and Italian Agip oil company.
- The European Commission to allocate some 2.5 million Ecu to assist the democratisation of the Croatian media. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
